sentences.zh: 列傳第七

translations.literal: Biographies 7
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 7

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣劉懷肅劉粹孫處蒯恩向靖劉鍾虞丘進孟懷玉胡藩劉康祖

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan, Liu Huaisu, Liu Cui, Sun Chu, Kuai En, Xiang Jing, Liu Zhong, Yu Qiujin, Meng Huaiyu, Hu Fan, Liu Kangzu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan, Liu Huaisu, Liu Cui, Sun Chu, Kuai En, Xiang Jing, Liu Zhong, Yu Qiujin, Meng Huaiyu, Hu Fan, and Liu Kangzu

sentences.zh: 刘敬宣，字万寿，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan, styled Wanshou, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan, courtesy name Wanshou, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父牢之，晋镇北将军。

translations.literal: His father Laozhi was Jin's General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Laozhi had served as General Who Pacifies the North under Jin.

sentences.zh: 敬宣八岁丧母，昼夜号泣，中表异之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan lost his mother at eight; day and night he wailed, and kin both near and far marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxuan was eight his mother died; he wept day and night until relatives near and far took notice.

sentences.zh: 辅国将军桓序镇芜湖，牢之参序军事。

translations.literal: Auxiliary-state General Huan Xu garrisoned Wuhu; Laozhi served on Xu's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Auxiliary-state General Huan Xu held Wuhu, and Laozhi joined his military staff.

sentences.zh: 四月八日，敬宣见众人灌佛，乃下头上金镜为母灌像，因悲泣不自胜。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month Jingxuan saw the crowd bathing the Buddha; he took the gold mirror from his head and used it to bathe an image for his mother, then wept beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month he watched others bathe Buddha images, removed the gold mirror from his own head to bathe one for his mother, and broke down in grief.

sentences.zh: 序谓牢之曰："卿此儿非唯家之孝子，必为国之忠臣。"

translations.literal: Xu said to Laozhi, "Your boy is not only a filial son of the house—he will surely be a loyal minister of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Xu told Laozhi, "This son of yours is not merely a filial son at home—he will become a loyal minister to the realm."

sentences.zh: 起家王恭前軍參軍，又參會稽世子元顯征虜軍事。

translations.literal: He began office as aide in Wang Gong's vanguard army, then served on Kuaiji Heir Apparent Yuanxian's staff against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an aide in Wang Gong's vanguard, then joined the staff of Kuaiji heir Yuanxian on the campaign against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 隆安二年，王恭起兵京口，以誅司馬尚之為名，牢之時為恭前軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Long'an Wang Gong raised troops at Jingkou in the name of executing Sima Shangzhi; Laozhi was then Gong's vanguard marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an year 2 Wang Gong mobilized at Jingkou, claiming he meant to execute Sima Shangzhi; Laozhi was his vanguard marshal.

sentences.zh: 恭以豪戚自居，甚相陵忽，牢之心不能平。

translations.literal: Gong treated himself as a great kinsman and looked down on others greatly; Laozhi's heart could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gong acted the proud magnate and treated Laozhi with open contempt, which Laozhi could not stomach.

sentences.zh: 及恭此舉，使牢之為前鋒，牢之遣敬宣襲恭，敗之。

translations.literal: When Gong made this move he had Laozhi lead the van; Laozhi sent Jingxuan to strike Gong and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong marched, Laozhi was put at the head of the army; he sent Jingxuan to surprise Gong and routed him.

sentences.zh: 元顯以敬宣為後將軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Yuanxian made Jingxuan rear-general advising aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian appointed Jingxuan advising aide to the rear general.

sentences.zh: 三年，孫恩為亂，牢之自表東討，敬宣請以騎傍南山趣其後。

translations.literal: In the third year Sun En rebelled; Laozhi memorialized himself to campaign east, and Jingxuan asked to take cavalry along the southern hills to hit their rear.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, when Sun En rose in revolt, Laozhi volunteered to campaign in the east and Jingxuan proposed flanking the rebels with cavalry along the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 吳賊畏馬，又懼首尾受敵，遂大敗之，進平會稽。

translations.literal: The Wu bandits feared horses and also feared attack front and rear, so they were greatly defeated; he advanced and pacified Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu rebels feared cavalry and dreaded being caught between two forces; they were routed, and the army went on to pacify Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 遷後軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to aide in the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to aide in the rear army.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝既累破祅賊，功名日盛，敬宣深相憑結。

translations.literal: Song Emperor Wu had repeatedly broken the demon rebels and his fame grew daily; Jingxuan deeply attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Wu of Song kept crushing the rebel cults and his renown rose, Jingxuan drew close to him.

sentences.zh: 元顯進號驃騎，敬宣仍隨府轉。

translations.literal: Yuanxian advanced in title to Flying Cavalry General; Jingxuan still followed the headquarters in transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanxian took the title Flying Cavalry General, Jingxuan moved with his staff.

sentences.zh: 元顯驕肆，群下化之，敬宣每預宴會，調戲無所酬答，元顯甚不悅。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was arrogant and unrestrained, and his subordinates took their cue from him; whenever Jingxuan joined banquets he offered no witty replies to their teasing, and Yuanxian was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was insolent and his courtiers followed suit; at feasts Jingxuan never played along with their jibes, which Yuanxian resented.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，牢之南討桓玄，元顯為征討大都督，日夜昏酣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing Laozhi campaigned south against Huan Xuan; Yuanxian was grand commander of the punitive force and day and night drowned himself in wine.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing year 1 Laozhi marched south against Huan Xuan while Yuanxian, supreme commander of the expedition, spent his days and nights in drunken stupor.

sentences.zh: 牢之以道子昏闇，元顯淫凶，慮平玄之日，亂政方始；

translations.literal: Laozhi thought Daozi benighted and Yuanxian lewd and cruel, and feared that once Xuan was pacified misrule would only begin.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi saw Daozi as dim-witted and Yuanxian as vicious and debauched, and worried that defeating Xuan would merely usher in worse disorder.

sentences.zh: 會玄遣信說牢之，牢之欲假手于玄誅執政，然後乘玄之隙，可以得志天下。

translations.literal: When Xuan sent envoys to win Laozhi, Laozhi wished to borrow Xuan's hand to kill those in power, then exploit Xuan's gap and realize his ambition under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent messengers to sway him; Laozhi planned to use Xuan to destroy the ruling clique, then strike when Xuan slipped and seize power for himself.

sentences.zh: 將許玄降。

translations.literal: He was about to agree to surrender to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of submitting to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 敬宣諫恐玄威望既成，則難圖。

translations.literal: Jingxuan remonstrated, fearing that once Xuan's prestige was established he would be hard to overthrow.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan warned that if Xuan's authority solidified, he would be impossible to remove.

sentences.zh: 牢之怒曰：「吾豈不知今日取之如反復手，但平後令我奈驃騎何？

translations.literal: Laozhi angrily said, "Do I not know that taking him today is like turning the hand over—but after the victory what am I to do about the Flying Cavalry General?
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi snapped, "Of course I know beating him now is as easy as flipping my hand—but once it's done, how am I supposed to deal with the Flying Cavalry General?

sentences.zh: 」遣敬宣為任。

translations.literal: " He sent Jingxuan on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: " He dispatched Jingxuan to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 玄既得志，害元顯，廢道子，以牢之為會稽太守。

translations.literal: Once Xuan had his way he killed Yuanxian, deposed Daozi, and made Laozhi Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan seized power he executed Yuanxian, deposed Daozi, and appointed Laozhi administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 牢之與敬宣謀襲玄，期以明旦。

translations.literal: Laozhi and Jingxuan plotted to strike Xuan, fixing the attack for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi and Jingxuan plotted a dawn assault on Xuan.

sentences.zh: 爾日大霧，府門晚開，日旰，敬宣不至。

translations.literal: That day thick fog hung; the headquarters gate opened late, the sun was low, and Jingxuan did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Thick fog delayed the opening of headquarters; the sun was setting and Jingxuan still had not come.

sentences.zh: 牢之謂謀泄，欲奔廣陵，而敬宣還京口迎家。

translations.literal: Laozhi thought the plot had leaked and wanted to flee to Guangling, while Jingxuan returned to Jingkou to fetch the family.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi assumed the plot was exposed and meant to flee to Guangling while Jingxuan went back to Jingkou for his household.

sentences.zh: 牢之謂已為玄禽，乃縊而死。

translations.literal: Laozhi thought he had already been taken by Xuan and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Xuan had already seized him, Laozhi hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 敬宣奔喪，哭畢，就司馬休之、高雅之等俱奔洛陽，往來長安，求救于姚興，後奔慕容德。

translations.literal: Jingxuan rushed to the funeral; when the mourning was done he joined Sima Xiuzhi, Gao Yazhi, and others in flight to Luoyang, then traveled to Chang'an to beg aid from Yao Xing, and later fled to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan returned for the burial; when rites were finished he fled with Sima Xiuzhi and Gao Yazhi to Luoyang and Chang'an seeking help from Yao Xing, then took refuge with Murong De.

sentences.zh: 敬宣素明天文，知必有興復晉室者。

translations.literal: Jingxuan had long understood astronomy and knew there must be one who would restore the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan was versed in astronomy and was sure someone would restore the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 尋夢丸土服之，覺而喜曰：「丸者，桓也，桓吞，吾當復本土乎。

translations.literal: Soon he dreamed he swallowed a pellet of earth and awoke, saying with joy, "A pellet is Huan; if Huan is swallowed, shall I not return to my native land?
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed he swallowed a ball of earth and woke saying, "A ball—huan—means Huan; if Huan is swallowed, will I not go home again?

sentences.zh: 」乃結青州大姓諸崔、封謀滅德，推休之為主。

translations.literal: " He then joined great Qingzhou clans Cui and Feng to destroy De and set up Xiuzhi as leader.
translations.idiomatic: " He then allied with leading Qingzhou families of the Cui and Feng to overthrow De and make Xiuzhi their chief.

sentences.zh: 時德司空劉軌大被任，高雅之又要軌，謀泄，乃相與殺軌而去。

translations.literal: At that time De's Minister of Works Liu Gui was greatly trusted; Yazhi also tried to win Gui, the plot leaked, and they killed Gui and fled together.
translations.idiomatic: De's minister of works Liu Gui enjoyed great favor; Yazhi tried to recruit him, the plot was exposed, and they murdered Gui and fled.

sentences.zh: 會宋武帝平京口，手書召敬宣，即馳還，襲封武岡縣男，後拜江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Song Emperor Wu pacified Jingkou he summoned Jingxuan by personal letter; Jingxuan galloped back, was enfeoffed Baron of Wugang, and later appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took Jingkou he wrote Jingxuan a personal summons; Jingxuan raced back, received the barony of Wugang, and later became inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉毅之少，人或以雄桀許之。

translations.literal: In Liu Yi's youth some called him a heroic champion.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth some hailed Liu Yi as a bold hero.

sentences.zh: 敬宣曰：「此人外寬內忌，自伐而尚人，若一旦遭逢，當以陵上取禍。

translations.literal: Jingxuan said, "This man is outwardly broad yet inwardly jealous, self-aggrandizing yet deferential to others; if he meets his moment he will bring disaster by overreaching his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan said, "He looks tolerant but broods within, boasts of himself yet flatters others; given the chance he will ruin himself by lording it over his betters.

sentences.zh: 」毅聞深恨。

translations.literal: " Yi heard and deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yi heard this he nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 及在江陵，知敬宣還，尋知為江州，大駭惋。

translations.literal: When he was at Jiangling and learned Jingxuan had returned, then learned he had become inspector of Jiangzhou, he was greatly shocked and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling, learning Jingxuan was back and now inspector of Jiangzhou, Yi was stunned and dismayed.

sentences.zh: 敬宣愈不自安。

translations.literal: Jingxuan grew ever more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan grew increasingly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 安帝反正，自表求解。

translations.literal: When Emperor An was restored Jingxuan memorialized asking to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor An was restored, Jingxuan asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 武帝恩款周洽，所賜莫與為比。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's kindness and favor were thorough; what he bestowed had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu treated him with unmatched warmth and generosity.

sentences.zh: 敬宣女嫁，賜錢三百萬，雜彩千匹。

translations.literal: When Jingxuan's daughter married he gave three million cash and a thousand bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingxuan's daughter's wedding he gave three million cash and a thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 帝方大相寵任，欲令立功。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then greatly favoring and trusting him and wanted him to win merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was lavishing favor on him and wanted him to earn glory in the field.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，表遣敬宣伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi he memorialized sending Jingxuan to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 3 he proposed sending Jingxuan against Shu.

sentences.zh: 博士周祗諫，以為「道遠運漕難繼，毛修之家讎不雪，不應以得死為恨。

translations.literal: Erudite Zhou Zhi remonstrated, saying, "The road is far and transport by water hard to sustain; Mao Xiuzhi's family blood-feud is unavenged—he should not treat death as regret.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhou Zhi objected: "The distance is great and supply lines fragile; Mao Xiuzhi's family vendetta remains unsettled—he ought not to march off expecting to die in vain.

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣蒙生存之恩，亦宜性命仰答。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan received the grace of life; he too should repay with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan owes you the debt of his life and should answer with his life in return.

sentences.zh: 將軍欲驅二死之甘心，忘國家之重計，愚情竊所未安」。

translations.literal: The general would drive two men willing to die and forget the weight of the state's plan—in my humble view this is what I cannot be at ease with."
translations.idiomatic: You would spend two lives eager for death and ignore the realm's larger design—I cannot reconcile myself to that."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 假敬宣節，監征蜀諸軍事。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was given credentials and put in charge of all forces against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan received imperial credentials and overall command of the Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 敬宣至黃武，去成都五百里，食盡，遇疾疫而還。

translations.literal: Jingxuan reached Huangwu, five hundred li from Chengdu; provisions ran out, plague struck, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan reached Huangwu, five hundred li from Chengdu, but food gave out and disease spread, forcing his retreat.

sentences.zh: 為有司奏免官。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五年，武帝伐慕容超，除中軍諮議參軍，與兗州刺史劉藩大破超軍，進圍廣固，屢獻規略。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Wu attacked Murong Chao; Jingxuan was made advising aide in the central army and with Yanzhou Inspector Liu Fan greatly defeated Chao's army, advanced to besiege Guanggu, and repeatedly offered plans.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, campaigning against Murong Chao, Jingxuan became an advising aide in the central army; with Liu Fan of Yanzhou he routed Chao and besieged Guanggu, offering strategy at every turn.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼建鄴，敬宣分領鮮卑獸斑突騎，置陣甚整。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed Jiankang Jingxuan separately commanded Xianbei beast-spotted shock cavalry and set the formation very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened Jiankang, Jingxuan led Xianbei cavalry with spotted mounts and drew up an impeccable line.

sentences.zh: 循走，仍從南討，為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Xun fled; he still followed the southern campaign and became General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun fled he continued south and was made General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 敬宣寬厚，善待士，多伎藝，弓馬音律，無事不善。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was generous, treated scholars well, and had many skills—in archery, horsemanship, and music there was nothing he did not excel at.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and gracious to men of talent, he mastered archery, horsemanship, music—there was scarcely an art he could not handle.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射謝混美才地，少所交納，與敬宣遇便盡禮。

translations.literal: Secretary Deputy Director Xie Hun had fine talent and standing and rarely made new acquaintances; with Jingxuan he at once showed full courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hun, vice director of the secretariat, seldom befriended anyone, yet with Jingxuan he was immediately cordial.

sentences.zh: 或問混：「卿未嘗輕交，而傾蓋劉壽，何也？

translations.literal: Someone asked Hun, "You have never lightly befriended anyone, yet you treat Liu Shou with open arms—why?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Hun, "You rarely open up to people—why this instant bond with Liu Shou?

sentences.zh: 」混曰：「孔文舉禮太史子義，天下豈有非之邪。」

translations.literal: " Hun said, "Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi—did anyone under heaven fault him for it?"
translations.idiomatic: " Hun replied, "When Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi, who in the realm criticized him?"

sentences.zh: 初，敬宣蜀還，劉毅欲以重法繩之。

translations.literal: At first, when Jingxuan returned from Shu, Liu Yi wanted to punish him by heavy law.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxuan came back from Shu, Liu Yi wanted him punished severely.

sentences.zh: 武帝既相任待，又何無忌謂不宜以私憾傷至公。

translations.literal: The Emperor already trusted and employed him, and He Wuji said one should not let private resentment harm supreme fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already relied on him, and He Wuji argued that private spite must not override the public good.

sentences.zh: 毅雖止，猶謂武帝曰：「平生之舊，豈可孤信？

translations.literal: Although Yi stopped, he still said to the Emperor, "An old friend of many years—can he be trusted alone?
translations.idiomatic: Yi desisted, yet told the emperor, "A companion of long standing—can you trust him blindly?

sentences.zh: 光武悔之于龐萌，曹公失之于孟卓。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu regretted Pang Meng; Cao Cao lost out with Meng Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu regretted trusting Pang Meng; Cao Cao was betrayed by Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 宜深慎之。

translations.literal: You should be deeply cautious."
translations.idiomatic: You should be very careful."

sentences.zh: 」毅出為荊州，謂敬宣曰：「欲屈卿為長史、南蠻，豈有見輔意乎？

translations.literal: " Yi went out to Jing Province and said to Jingxuan, "I wish to appoint you chief aide and southern barbarian commander—do you mean to assist me?
translations.idiomatic: " Posted to Jing Province, Yi told Jingxuan, "I want you as chief aide and commander of the southern barbarians—will you serve under me?

sentences.zh: 」敬宣懼禍，以告武帝。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan feared disaster and told the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Fearing a trap, Jingxuan reported this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「但令老兄平安，必無過慮。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Only let your old brother stay safe and you need not worry too much.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed: "So long as your old friend keeps his head, you have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」後領冀州刺史。

translations.literal: " Later he held the post of Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Jingxuan became inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 時帝西討劉毅，豫州刺史諸葛長人監太尉軍事，貽敬宣書曰：「盤龍狼戾專恣，自取夷滅。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned west against Liu Yi, Yuzhou Inspector Zhuge Changren supervised the Grand Marshal's military affairs and wrote Jingxuan, "Panlong was wolfish, wilful, and brought ruin on himself.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor marched west against Liu Yi, Zhuge Changren of Yuzhou, overseeing the grand marshal's armies, wrote Jingxuan: "Panlong's arrogance destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 異端將盡，世路方夷，富貴之事，相與共之。

translations.literal: The strange branch is nearly gone and the world's path is clearing; matters of wealth and honor let us share them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel faction is almost finished and better days lie ahead—let us share the rewards together.

sentences.zh: 」敬宣報曰：「下官常懼福過災生，實思避盈居損。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan replied, "This humble officer has always feared fortune outrunning merit and truly wishes to avoid fullness and dwell in modesty.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan answered, "I have always feared that good luck invites disaster and sought to stay modest rather than grasp for more.

sentences.zh: 富貴之旨，非所敢當。

translations.literal: The intent of wealth and honor is not what I dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept such an offer of rank and riches.

sentences.zh: 」便以長人書呈，帝謂王誕曰：「阿壽故為不負我。」

translations.literal: " He at once presented Changren's letter; the Emperor said to Wang Dan, "A Shou truly does not fail me."
translations.idiomatic: " He forwarded Changren's letter at once; the emperor told Wang Dan, "A Shou has not let me down."

sentences.zh: 十一年，進號右軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he advanced in title to General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was promoted to General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 時晉宗室司馬道賜為敬宣參軍。

translations.literal: At that time Jin clansman Sima Daosi was Jingxuan's staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jin imperial clansman Sima Daosi then served on Jingxuan's staff.

sentences.zh: 會武帝西征司馬休之，而道賜乃陰結同府辟閭道秀、左右小將王猛子等謀反。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Daosi secretly joined staff member Pilu Daoxiu and junior officers Wang Mengzi and others in plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: During the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Daosi secretly conspired with staff officer Pilu Daoxiu and aides Wang Mengzi and others.

sentences.zh: 道賜自號齊王，規據廣固，舉兵應休之。

translations.literal: Daosi styled himself Prince of Qi, planned to hold Guanggu, and raised troops to support Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Daosi proclaimed himself Prince of Qi, aimed to seize Guanggu, and mustered forces for Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 猛子取敬宣刀殺敬宣，文武佐吏即討道賜、道秀、猛子斬之。

translations.literal: Mengzi took Jingxuan's sword and killed Jingxuan; civil and military aides at once punished Daosi, Daoxiu, and Mengzi and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzi seized Jingxuan's sword and killed him; staff and officers immediately executed Daosi, Daoxiu, and Mengzi.

sentences.zh: 先是敬宣嘗夜與僚佐宴，空中有投一隻芒屩於坐，墜敬宣食盤上，長三尺五寸，已經人著，耳鼻間並欲壞，頃之而敗。

translations.literal: Earlier Jingxuan had once feasted at night with his staff; from the air someone threw a single straw sandal onto the seat—it fell into Jingxuan's food tray, three chi five cun long, already worn by a person, nose and ears nearly ruined—and soon after he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a night feast with his officers, a worn straw sandal three feet five inches long—reeking of a human wearer—dropped from nowhere into his dish; not long after he was killed.

sentences.zh: 喪至，武帝臨哭甚哀。

translations.literal: When the coffin arrived the Emperor came in person to mourn, very sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: When the bier arrived the emperor mourned him in person, deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 子光祖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Guangzu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guangzu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Song took the throne the enfeoffment lapsed.

sentences.zh: 劉懷肅，彭城人，宋武帝從母兄也。

translations.literal: Liu Huaisu was a man of Pengcheng, maternal elder cousin to Song Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaisu of Pengcheng was the emperor's cousin on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 家世貧窶，而躬耕好學。

translations.literal: The family had long been poor, yet he personally plowed and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was poor he farmed himself and loved study.

sentences.zh: 仕晉為費令。

translations.literal: He served Jin as magistrate of Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin he served as magistrate of Fei county.

sentences.zh: 及聞武帝起義，棄縣來奔。

translations.literal: When he heard the Emperor had raised the banner of revolt he abandoned his county and came to join.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the emperor had risen in arms, he abandoned his post and rushed to join him.

sentences.zh: 蔚祖卒，子道存嗣，位太尉江夏王義恭諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Weizu died; his son Daocun succeeded, reaching the post of advising aide to Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu died; his son Daocun succeeded and rose to advising aide to Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 孝武伐元凶，道存出奔義軍，元凶乃殺其母以徇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu attacked the crown prince's killer, Daocun fled to the loyalist army; the killer executed his mother as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched against the usurper, Daocun defected to the loyalists; the usurper killed his mother as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 景和中，為義恭太宰從事中郎。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era he became aide to Prince Yigong as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinghe reign he served as aide to Prince Yigong in his role as grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 義恭敗，以黨與下獄死。

translations.literal: When Yigong fell he was imprisoned as a partisan and died in jail.
translations.idiomatic: After Yigong's downfall he was jailed as an accomplice and died there.

sentences.zh: 懷肅次弟懷敬，澀訥無才能。

translations.literal: Huaisu's next younger brother Huaijing was dull-spoken and without talent.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu's younger brother Huaijing was slow of speech and lacked ability.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝產而皇妣殂，孝皇帝貧薄，無由得乳人，議欲不舉，帝從母生懷敬，未期，乃斷懷敬乳而自養帝。

translations.literal: At first when the Emperor was born the imperial mother died; Emperor Xiao was poor and had no wet nurse; they debated not raising the child; the Emperor's maternal aunt bore Huaijing, not yet weaned, so she stopped Huaijing's milk and nursed the Emperor herself.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor was born his mother died; the household was too poor for a wet nurse and nearly abandoned the infant until his aunt, still nursing Huaijing, weaned her own son to feed him.

sentences.zh: 帝以舊恩，懷敬累見寵授，至會稽太守。

translations.literal: Because of the old kindness the Emperor repeatedly favored Huaijing, reaching Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Out of gratitude for that old debt the emperor kept advancing Huaijing until he became administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 時以為速，武帝曰：「亡姨于我恩重，此何可忘？

translations.literal: People then thought it too fast; the Emperor said, "My late aunt's kindness to me was heavy—how could this be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: Critics called the promotions too swift; the emperor said, "My aunt's kindness was profound—how could I forget it?

sentences.zh: 」曆尚書，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " He served as Minister of the Masters of Writing and as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on to serve as minister of the masters of writing and as grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 懷敬子真道為錢唐令，元嘉十三年，東土饑，帝遣揚州中從事史沈演之巡行在所，演之表真道及余杭令劉道錫有美政。

translations.literal: Huaijing's son Zhendao was magistrate of Qiantang; in the thirteenth year of Yuanjia the eastern lands suffered famine and the Emperor sent Yangzhou aide-on-duty Shen Yanzhi to tour the region; Yanzhi memorialized that Zhendao and Yuhang magistrate Liu Daoxi had excellent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing's son Zhendao was magistrate of Qiantang; in Yuanjia 13, when famine struck the east, Shen Yanzhi reported that Zhendao and Liu Daoxi of Yuhang governed admirably.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，各賜穀千斛，以真道為步兵校尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this and to each gave a thousand hu of grain; Zhendao was made Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded each with a thousand hu of grain and made Zhendao commandant of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was sent out as inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 十八年，氐帥楊難當侵寇漢中，真道討破之，而難當寇盜猶不已，文帝遣龍驤將軍裴方明率禁兵五千，受真道節度。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Di chieftain Yang Dang invaded Hanzhong; Zhendao defeated him, yet Dang's raids did not cease; Emperor Wen sent Flying Dragon General Pei Fangming with five thousand palace troops under Zhendao's command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 the Di leader Yang Dang raided Hanzhong; Zhendao beat him back but raids continued, so Emperor Wen sent Pei Fangming with five thousand imperial troops under Zhendao's orders.

sentences.zh: 十九年，方明至武興，率太子積弩將軍劉康祖等進軍，大致克捷，以真道為建威將軍、雍州刺史，方明輔國將軍、梁南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Fangming reached Wuxing and with Crown Prince crossbow General Liu Kangzu and others advanced; great victory followed; Zhendao was made General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yongzhou, Fangming Assistant-state General and Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 Fangming reached Wuxing and marched with Liu Kangzu and others to a sweeping victory; Zhendao became General Who Establishes Might and inspector of Yongzhou, Fangming assistant-state general and inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 又詔故晉壽太守姜道盛殞身鋒鏑，可贈給事中，賜錢十萬。

translations.literal: The edict also said former Jinshou Administrator Jiang Daosheng died at the spear-point and should be given Palace Attendant and a hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also honored the late Jinshou administrator Jiang Daosheng, killed in battle, with the post of palace attendant and a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 道盛注古文尚書行于世。

translations.literal: Daosheng annotated the Old Text Book of Documents and it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng had annotated the Old Text Book of Documents, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 真道、方明並坐破仇池斷割金銀諸雜寶貨，又藏難當善馬，下獄死。

translations.literal: Zhendao and Fangming were both punished for seizing gold, silver, and other treasures when Qiu Chi fell and for hiding Yang Dang's fine horses; they died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendao and Fangming were executed for looting gold and silver at Qiu Chi and concealing Yang Dang's best horses.

sentences.zh: 懷敬弟懷慎，少謹慎質直。

translations.literal: Huaijing's younger brother Huaishen in youth was cautious, honest, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing's younger brother Huaishen was cautious and plain-spoken from youth.

sentences.zh: 從宋武帝征討，位徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Song Emperor Wu on campaigns and reached the post of Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Emperor Wu and rose to inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴猛，境內震肅。

translations.literal: His governance was stern and fierce; within the circuit all were awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with harsh discipline and kept the region in awe-struck order.

sentences.zh: 以平廣固、盧循功，封南城縣男。

translations.literal: For pacifying Guanggu and Lu Xun he was enfeoffed Baron of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: For victories at Guanggu and over Lu Xun he received the barony of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，武帝北伐，以為中領軍、征虜將軍，宿衛輦轂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year when the Emperor marched north he was made Central Camp Commander and General Who Subdues the Barbarians, guarding the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, during the northern campaign, he became central camp commander and General Who Subdues the Barbarians, guarding the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 坐府內相殺免官。

translations.literal: He was removed from office for killings within his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after a fatal brawl inside headquarters.

sentences.zh: 雖名位轉優，而恭恪愈至。

translations.literal: Though name and rank grew ever higher, his reverence grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: The higher his rank rose, the more deferential he became.

sentences.zh: 每所之造，位任不踰己者，皆束帶門外下車，其謹退類如此。

translations.literal: Whenever he visited anyone whose position did not exceed his own, he would gird himself, get down from his carriage outside the gate, and wait—so cautious and retiring was he.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting anyone of equal or lower rank, he belted up and dismounted outside the gate—such was his humility.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，以佐命功，進爵為侯，位五兵尚書，加散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, for merit in founding the dynasty, he was advanced to marquis, made Minister of the Five Armies, and given concurrent posts as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 1, for founding merit, he was raised to marquis, made minister of the five armies, and given concurrent posts as regular attendant and Bright Hall grand master.

sentences.zh: 景平元年，遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping he was moved to General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingping 1 he became General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 祿賜班於宗族，家無餘財，卒諡肅侯。

translations.literal: Stipends and gifts he distributed among his clan; the house held no surplus wealth; on death he was titled Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: He shared stipends with his kin and died without private wealth; his posthumous title was Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 德願善御車，嘗立兩柱，使其中劣通車軸，乃于百餘步上振轡長驅，未至數尺，打牛奔從柱間直過，其精如此。

translations.literal: Deyuan was skilled at driving carriages; he once set up two posts with barely enough space for an axle between them, then from over a hundred paces whipped up at full gallop; within a few feet he drove the ox to bolt straight through the gap—such was his precision.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan excelled at charioteering: he erected two posts barely wider than an axle, then from a hundred paces charged full speed and threaded the gap within inches—such was his skill.

sentences.zh: 孝武聞其能，為之乘畫輪車，幸太宰江夏王義恭第。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu heard of his ability and had him drive the painted-wheel carriage when visiting Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, hearing of his skill, had him drive the painted imperial carriage on a visit to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 德願岸著籠冠，短朱衣，執轡進止，甚有容狀。

translations.literal: Deyuan wore a tall cage-cap and short vermilion coat, holding the reins with stately bearing in advance and halt.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a tall cage-cap and short red coat, managing reins and pace with dignified poise.

sentences.zh: 永光中，為廷尉，與柳元景厚善。

translations.literal: In the Yongguang era he was Minister of Justice and thick friends with Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongguang he served as minister of justice and was close to Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 元景敗，下獄誅。

translations.literal: When Yuanjing fell he was imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanjing fell he was jailed and put to death.

sentences.zh: 懷慎庶長子榮祖，少好騎射，為武帝所知。

translations.literal: Huaishen's eldest son by a concubine, Rongzu, from youth loved riding and shooting and was noticed by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen's eldest concubine-born son Rongzu loved horsemanship and archery and caught the emperor's eye.

sentences.zh: 及盧循攻逼，時賊乘小艦入淮拔柵，武帝宣令三軍不得輒射賊。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the attack, the rebels took small boats into the Huai to pull up palisades; the Emperor ordered the three armies not to shoot the enemy without leave.
translations.idiomatic: During Lu Xun's assault rebels rowed small boats up the Huai to tear out stakes; the emperor forbade the armies to shoot without orders.

sentences.zh: 榮祖不勝憤怒，冒禁射之，所中應弦而倒，帝益奇焉。

translations.literal: Rongzu could not contain his anger, violated the ban and shot; those hit fell at the twang of the string, and the Emperor admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu, furious, defied the order and shot; every arrow found its mark, and the emperor admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 以戰功，參太尉軍事，從討司馬休之。

translations.literal: For battle merit he joined the Grand Marshal's staff and followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: For battlefield merit he joined the grand marshal's staff on the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 彭城內史徐逵之敗沒，諸將意沮，榮祖請戰愈厲，上乃解所著鎧授之。

translations.literal: When Pengcheng interior minister Xu Daizhi was defeated and lost, the generals' spirits sank; Rongzu asked to fight all the more fiercely, and the Emperor took off his own armor and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Daizhi's defeat dampened morale, Rongzu begged to fight harder; the emperor stripped off his own armor and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 榮祖陷陣，身被數創。

translations.literal: Rongzu broke the enemy line and received many wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu punched through the line, covered in wounds.

sentences.zh: 及帝北伐，轉鎮西中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched north he was transferred to middle army aide in the west garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern expedition he became middle army aide in the western command.

sentences.zh: 水軍入河，與朱超石大破魏軍於半城。

translations.literal: The navy entered the Yellow River and with Zhu Chao shi greatly defeated Wei forces at Bancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet entered the Yellow River and, with Zhu Chao shi, routed Wei at Bancheng.

sentences.zh: 帝大饗戰士，謂榮祖曰：「卿以寡克眾，攻無堅城，雖古名將何以過此。

translations.literal: The Emperor feasted the warriors greatly and said to Rongzu, "You with few overcame many and took every stronghold you assaulted—even ancient famous generals could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting the troops the emperor told Rongzu, "You beat larger forces and cracked every fortress—no ancient general could do better.

sentences.zh: 」永初中，為輔國將軍。

translations.literal: " In the beginning of Yongchu he was made Assistant-state General.
translations.idiomatic: " In early Yongchu he was made assistant-state general.

sentences.zh: 追論半城功，賜爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Recalling merit at Bancheng, he was given the barony of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His Bancheng victory earned him the barony of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 榮祖為人輕財貴義，善撫將士；

translations.literal: Rongzu as a man lightly valued wealth and prized righteousness, and kindly led soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu scorned money, honored duty, and treated soldiers generously;

sentences.zh: 然性褊，頗失士君子心。

translations.literal: yet his nature was narrow and he rather lost the hearts of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was touchy and lost the respect of refined men.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 懷慎弟懷默，江夏內史。

translations.literal: Huaishen's younger brother Huuaimo was interior minister of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishen's brother Huuaimo served as interior minister of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 子孫登，武陵內史。

translations.literal: His descendant Deng was interior minister of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant Deng became interior minister of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 孫登子亮，少工刀楯，以軍功封順陽縣侯，曆梁、益二州刺史。

translations.literal: Deng's son Liang from youth was skilled with blade and shield; for military merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Shunyang and served as Inspector of Liang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's son Liang mastered sword and shield from youth; for merit he became marquis of Shunyang and inspector of Liang and Yi.

sentences.zh: 在任廉儉，所得公祿，悉以還官，宋明帝下詔褒美。

translations.literal: In office he was frugal; all official salary he returned to the state; Emperor Ming of Song issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal in office, he remitted his salary to the treasury; Emperor Ming praised him by edict.

sentences.zh: 亮在梁州忽服食，欲致長生，迎武當山道士孫懷道使合仙藥，藥成，服之而卒。

translations.literal: Liang in Liangzhou suddenly took elixirs seeking long life, welcomed a Wudang mountain Daoist Sun Huaidao to compound an immortal drug, took it when ready, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Liangzhou Liang turned to alchemy for immortality, summoned Daoist Sun Huaidao from Mount Wudang to brew a elixir, swallowed it, and died.

sentences.zh: 及就斂，屍弱如生。

translations.literal: At encoffining the corpse was soft as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: At burial his body was still supple as though alive.

sentences.zh: 諡曰剛侯。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Marquis Gang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Marquis Gang.

sentences.zh: 孫登弟道隆，前廢帝景和中，位右衛將軍，封永昌縣侯，委以腹心之任。

translations.literal: Deng's younger brother Daolong, in the Jinghe era of the deposed emperor, was General of the Right Guard, enfeoffed Marquis of Yongchang, and entrusted with intimate confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's brother Daolong, under the deposed emperor in Jinghe, was General of the Right Guard, marquis of Yongchang, and a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，又為明帝盡力，遷左衛將軍、中護軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Taishi he again exerted himself for Emperor Ming and was moved to General of the Left Guard and Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taishi he served Emperor Ming loyally and rose to General of the Left Guard and Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 賜死，事在建安王休仁傳。

translations.literal: He was ordered to die; the affair is in the biography of Prince Xiuren of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was condemned to death; the affair is recorded in the biography of Prince Xiuren of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 劉粹字道沖，沛郡蕭人也。

translations.literal: Liu Cui, styled Daochong, was a man of Xiao in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cui, courtesy name Daochong, came from Xiao in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 家在京口。

translations.literal: The family resided at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The family lived at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 初為州從事，從宋武帝平建鄴，征廣固，以功封西安縣五等侯。

translations.literal: At first he was a commandery aide; he followed Song Emperor Wu in pacifying Jiankang and campaigning at Guanggu, and for merit was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a commandery aide, followed the emperor in taking Jiankang and Guanggu, and for merit received the fifth-rank marquisate of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 累遷中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to advising aide in the central army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to advising aide in the central army.

sentences.zh: 盧循之逼，京口任重，文帝時年四歲，武帝使粹奉文帝鎮京口。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed close, Jingkou's burden was heavy; Emperor Wen was then four years old and the Emperor had Cui attend Prince Wen at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened Jingkou the post was critical; the four-year-old Prince Wen was placed under Cui's care there.

sentences.zh: 後為江夏相。

translations.literal: Later he became Chancellor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He later became chancellor of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 族兄毅貳于武帝，粹不與毅同而盡心武帝。

translations.literal: Clansman Yi turned against the Emperor; Cui did not join Yi but gave his heart to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Liu Yi rebelled, but Cui stayed loyal to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝將謀毅，眾並疑粹在夏口，帝愈信之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to plot against Yi all together doubted Cui at Xiakou; the Emperor trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Planning to move against Yi, courtiers feared Cui at Xiakou, yet the emperor trusted him more.

sentences.zh: 及大軍至，竭其誠力。

translations.literal: When the great army arrived he exhausted his loyal strength.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force arrived he gave everything he had.

sentences.zh: 事平，封灄陽縣男。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was enfeoffed Baron of Sheng Yang.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he received the barony of Sheng Yang.

sentences.zh: 永初元年，以佐命功，改封建安縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, for founding merit, he was changed to Marquis of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 1, for founding merit, his fief became the marquisate of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，為雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne Cui became Inspector of Yong and was given overall command.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Wen's accession Cui became inspector of Yong with overall command.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，討謝晦。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he campaigned against Xie Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 3 he marched against Xie Hui.

sentences.zh: 初，晦與粹善，以粹子曠之為參軍，至是帝甚疑之。

translations.literal: At first Hui and Cui were on good terms and Hui made Cui's son Kuangzhi a staff officer; now the Emperor was very suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Cui had been friends and Hui had taken Cui's son Kuangzhi on staff; now the emperor was deeply wary.

sentences.zh: 王弘曰：「粹無私，必無憂也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong said, "Cui has no private ends—surely there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong said, "Cui is selfless—there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」及受命南討，一無所顧。

translations.literal: " When he received orders for the southern punitive campaign he showed not a trace of hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: " Ordered south against Hui he showed not a flicker of hesitation.

sentences.zh: 文帝以此嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 晦亦不害曠之，遣還。

translations.literal: Hui also did not harm Kuangzhi and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Hui did not harm Kuangzhi and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 粹尋卒，曠之嗣。

translations.literal: Cui soon died; Kuangzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Cui soon died; Kuangzhi inherited.

sentences.zh: 粹弟道濟，位益州刺史，任長史費謙等聚斂，傷政害人。

translations.literal: Cui's younger brother Daoji was Inspector of Yi; Chief Aide Fei Qian and others amassed wealth, harming governance and people.
translations.idiomatic: Cui's brother Daoji, inspector of Yi, let chief aide Fei Qian and others extort the people and ruin administration.

sentences.zh: 初，晉末有司馬飛龍者，自稱晉宗室，走仇池。

translations.literal: At first in late Jin there was Sima Feilong who styled himself a Jin clansman and fled to Qiu Chi.
translations.idiomatic: In late Jin a man named Sima Feilong claimed imperial descent and fled to Qiu Chi.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，聞道濟綏撫失和，遂自仇池入綿竹為亂，道濟遣軍討斬之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia, hearing Daoji's pacification was discordant, he entered Mianzhu from Qiu Chi and rebelled; Daoji sent troops who hunted and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 9, hearing Daoji's rule had turned harsh, he slipped from Qiu Chi into Mianzhu in revolt; Daoji's troops hunted him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 先是道濟以五城人帛氐奴、梁顯為參軍督護，費謙固執不與；

translations.literal: Earlier Daoji had made Wucheng men Bo Dinu and Liang Xian staff officers and supervisors; Fei Qian stubbornly refused to approve;
translations.idiomatic: Daoji had appointed Bo Dinu and Liang Xian of Wucheng as staff officers; Fei Qian blocked the appointments;

sentences.zh: 遠方商人至者，謙又抑之。

translations.literal: when distant merchants arrived Qian also held them back.
translations.idiomatic: and he also obstructed traveling merchants.

sentences.zh: 商旅呼嗟，百姓咸欲為亂，氐奴等因聚黨為盜，及趙廣等詐言司馬殿下猶在陽泉山中。

translations.literal: Travelers lamented and common people all wished to rebel; Dinu and others therefore gathered gangs as bandits, and Zhao Guang and others falsely claimed the Sima prince was still in Yangquan mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants groaned and the people seethed; Dinu and others turned bandit while Zhao Guang spread word that a Sima prince still hid on Mount Yangquan.

sentences.zh: 蜀土僑舊翕然並反，奉道人程道養，言是飛龍。

translations.literal: Shu émigrés and old families rose together, acclaiming the Daoist Cheng Daoyang, who claimed to be Feilong.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees and old families of Shu rose as one, proclaiming Daoist Cheng Daoyang as Feilong reborn.

sentences.zh: 道養，枹罕人也。

translations.literal: Daoyang was a man of Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyang came from Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 趙廣改名為龍興，號為蜀王、車騎大將軍、益梁二州牧，建號泰始元年，備置百官，以道養弟道助為驃騎將軍、長沙王，鎮涪城。

translations.literal: Zhao Guang changed his name to Longxing, styled himself King of Shu, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Governor of Yi and Liang, set the era name Taishi year 1, established the full bureaucracy, and made Daoyang's brother Daozhu Flying Cavalry General and Prince of Changsha, garrisoning Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guang renamed himself Longxing, crowned himself King of Shu and governor of Yi and Liang, dated his reign Taishi year 1, filled out a court, and made Daoyang's brother Daozhu flying cavalry general and Prince of Changsha at Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 廣自號鎮軍將軍，帛氐奴為征虜將軍，梁顯為鎮北將軍，奉道養圍成都。

translations.literal: Guang styled himself General Who Pacifies the Army; Bo Dinu was General Who Subdues the Barbarians; Liang Xian General Who Pacifies the North; they supported Daoyang in besieging Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Guang took the title General Who Pacifies the Army; Dinu and Xian became generals; together they besieged Chengdu for Daoyang.

sentences.zh: 道濟遣中兵參軍裴方明頻破之。

translations.literal: Daoji sent middle army aide Pei Fangming who repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji sent Pei Fangming, who routed them again and again.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，賊復大至，攻逼成都，道濟卒，方明等共埋屍於後齋，使書與道濟相似者為教。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year the rebels came again in force, pressing Chengdu; Daoji died; Fangming and others jointly buried the corpse in the rear study and had someone write orders resembling Daoji's hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 10 rebels swarmed Chengdu; Daoji died; Fangming buried him secretly in the rear hall and forged orders in his hand.

sentences.zh: 酬答簽疏，不異常日，雖母妻不知也。

translations.literal: Replies to documents were no different from ordinary days—even mother and wife did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Official correspondence continued as if nothing had changed—even his wife and mother were kept in the dark.

sentences.zh: 二月，道養升壇郊天，方就柴燎，方明擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the second month Daoyang ascended the altar to sacrifice to Heaven; just as the firewood was lit Fangming struck and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, as Daoyang lit the sacrificial fire on heaven's altar, Fangming attacked and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 會平西將軍臨川王義慶使巴東太守周籍之帥眾援成都，廣等屯據廣漢，分守郫川。

translations.literal: Pacifying-west General Prince Yiqing of Linchuan sent Badong Administrator Zhou Jizhi to lead troops to relieve Chengdu; Guang and others held Guanghan and divided forces to guard Pixian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiqing of Linchuan sent Zhou Jizhi of Badong to relieve Chengdu while Guang held Guanghan and split garrisons at Pixian.

sentences.zh: 籍之與方明攻郫，克之。

translations.literal: Jizhi and Fangming attacked Pixian and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi and Fangming stormed Pixian and took it.

sentences.zh: 方明禽偽驃騎將軍司馬龍伸，斬之。

translations.literal: Fangming captured the false Flying Cavalry General Sima Longshen and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming captured the rebel flying cavalry general Sima Longshen and executed him.

sentences.zh: 龍伸即道助也。

translations.literal: Longshen was Daozhu.
translations.idiomatic: Longshen was Daozhu.

sentences.zh: 涪、蜀皆平。

translations.literal: Fu and Shu were both pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Shu were both pacified.

sentences.zh: 俄而張尋攻破陰平，復與道養合，逃於郪山，其餘群賊出為盜不絕。

translations.literal: Soon Zhang Xun broke Yingping and again joined Daoyang, fleeing to Mount Xi; the remaining bandits raided without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Xun seized Yingping, rejoined Daoyang, and fled to Mount Xi while scattered rebels kept raiding.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣甯朔將軍蕭汪之討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent Pacifying-north General Xiao Wangzhi to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Xiao Wangzhi to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 十四年，餘党乃平，遷趙廣、張尋等於建鄴。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the remnant parties were finally pacified; Zhao Guang, Zhang Xun, and others were moved to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the last rebels were cleared; Guang and Zhang Xun were transferred to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，廣、尋復與國山令司馬敬琳謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Guang and Xun again plotted rebellion with Guoshan magistrate Sima Jinglin and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Guang and Xun conspired again with Sima Jinglin of Guoshan and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 粹族弟損字子騫，衛將軍毅從父弟也。

translations.literal: Cui's clansman Sun styled Ziqian was younger cousin to Guard General Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui's kinsman Sun, courtesy name Ziqian, was a younger cousin of Guard General Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 父鎮之字仲德，以毅貴顯，閒居京口，未嘗應召。

translations.literal: His father Zhenzhi, styled Zhongde, because Yi rose to glory lived retired at Jingkou and never answered summons.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhenzhi, styled Zhongde, retired at Jingkou when Yi grew powerful and never answered a summons.

sentences.zh: 常謂毅，「汝必破我家」。

translations.literal: He often told Yi, "You will surely ruin our house."
translations.idiomatic: He warned Yi repeatedly, "You will destroy our family."

sentences.zh: 毅甚畏憚，每還京口，未嘗敢以羽儀入鎮之門。

translations.literal: Yi greatly feared and respected him; whenever he returned to Jingkou he never dared enter Zhenzhi's gate with full guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi feared him; even at the height of power he never marched in full pomp through Zhenzhi's gate at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 以左光祿大夫征，不就，卒於家。

translations.literal: Summoned as Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall he did not go and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Bright Hall left grand master, he refused and died at home.

sentences.zh: 損元嘉中為吳郡太守，至昌門，便入太伯廟。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia Sun was Administrator of Wu commandery; reaching Chang Gate he at once entered the temple of the Grand Duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia, as administrator of Wu, Sun entered the Grand Duke's temple as soon as he reached Chang Gate.

sentences.zh: 時廟室頹毀，垣牆不修，損愴然曰：「清塵尚可髣佛，衡宇一何摧頹！

translations.literal: The shrine was then ruined, walls unrepaired; Sun said mournfully, "The pure dust can still be faintly seen—how utterly the halls have collapsed!
translations.idiomatic: The shrine lay in ruins; Sun sighed, "One can still faintly feel the old sanctity—yet how ruined the halls are!

sentences.zh: 」即令修葺。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered repairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered immediate repairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常。

translations.literal: On death he was given Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 損同郡宗人有劉伯龍者，少而貧薄，及長，歷位尚書左丞，少府，武陵太守，貧寠尤甚。

translations.literal: A clansman of the same commandery, Liu Bolong, was poor in youth; when grown he reached Left Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing, Minister of the Treasury, and Administrator of Wuling—yet remained extremely poor.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Liu Bolong grew up in poverty, rose to vice minister, treasury chief, and Wuling administrator, yet stayed miserably poor.

sentences.zh: 常在家慨然，召左右將營十一之方，忽見一鬼在傍撫掌大笑。

translations.literal: Often at home he sighed and summoned attendants to prepare an elixir of one-tenth; suddenly he saw a ghost at his side clapping and laughing.
translations.idiomatic: At home he sighed and told servants to brew an alchemical formula; a ghost appeared beside him and laughed.

sentences.zh: 伯龍歎曰：「貧窮固有命，乃復為鬼所笑也。

translations.literal: Bolong sighed, "Poverty truly has its fate—yet even a ghost mocks me.
translations.idiomatic: Bolong groaned, "Poverty is ordained—must even ghosts mock me?

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " He abandoned the attempt.

sentences.zh: 孫處字季高，會稽永興人也。

translations.literal: Sun Chu, styled Jigao, was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu, courtesy name Jigao, came from Yongxing in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 籍注字，故以字行。

translations.literal: Household register noted the style, so he was known by the style.
translations.idiomatic: The household register recorded his courtesy name, so he went by it.

sentences.zh: 少任氣，武帝征孫恩，季高樂從。

translations.literal: In youth he was spirited; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hot-blooded in youth, he eagerly joined the campaign against Sun En.

sentences.zh: 及平建鄴，封新夷縣五等侯。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiankang fell he received the fifth-rank marquisate of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 盧循之難，武帝謂季高曰：「此賊行破，非卿不能破其窟穴。

translations.literal: In Lu Xun's crisis the Emperor said to Jigao, "This bandit is about to break—only you can smash his nest.
translations.idiomatic: During Lu Xun's crisis the emperor told him, "This rebel is nearly finished—only you can destroy his lair.

sentences.zh: 」即遣季高泛海襲番禺，拔之。

translations.literal: " He at once sent Jigao by sea to strike Panyu and took it.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Jigao by sea against Panyu and captured it.

sentences.zh: 循父嘏、長史孫建之、司馬虞尪夫等輕舟奔始興，即分遣振武將軍沈田子等討平嶺表諸郡。

translations.literal: Xun's father Gu, Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi, and Marshal Yu Kuangfu and others fled in light boats to Shixing; he then sent General Who Quells the Barbarians Shen Tianzi and others to pacify the Lingnan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's father Gu, chief clerk Sun Jianzhi, and marshal Yu Kuangfu fled by light boat to Shixing; Jigao sent Shen Tianzi to pacify the southern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 循于左裏走還襲廣州，季高破走之。

translations.literal: Xun at Zuoli fled back to strike Guangzhou; Jigao defeated and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xun doubled back from Zuoli to hit Guangzhou; Jigao beat him off.

sentences.zh: 義熙七年，季高卒，追贈南海太守，封候官縣侯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi Jigao died; posthumously he was given Administrator of Nanhai and enfeoffed Marquis of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 7 Jigao died; posthumously he was made administrator of Nanhai and marquis of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 九年，武帝表贈交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor memorialized giving him the post of Inspector of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the emperor posthumously made him inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 蒯恩字道恩，蘭陵承人也。

translations.literal: Kuai En, styled Da'en, was a man of Cheng in Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai En, courtesy name Da'en, came from Cheng in Lanling.

sentences.zh: 武帝征孫恩，縣差恩伐馬芻，常負大束，兼倍餘人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Sun En the county assigned En to cut horse fodder; he often carried great bundles, twice others' load.
translations.idiomatic: When the county drafted him to cut fodder during the Sun En campaign, he carried double anyone else's load.

sentences.zh: 每舍芻於地，歎曰：「大丈夫彎弓三石，奈何充馬士。

translations.literal: Each time he set the fodder down he sighed, "A great man should bend a three-stone bow—why serve as horse groom?
translations.idiomatic: Dropping each bundle he muttered, "A real man draws a three-stone bow—why am I feeding horses?

sentences.zh: 」武帝聞之，即給器仗。

translations.literal: " The Emperor heard and at once gave him arms.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor heard and armed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 自征祅賊，常為先登，膽力過人，甚見愛信。

translations.literal: From campaigns against demon rebels he was always first to climb; courage and strength surpassed others and he was greatly loved and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight against the cult rebels he led the charge; his courage won deep trust.

sentences.zh: 于婁縣戰，箭中右目。

translations.literal: At Yuxian battle an arrow struck his right eye.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuxian an arrow pierced his right eye.

sentences.zh: 平京城，定建鄴，以軍功封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Pacifying the capital and settling Jiankang, for military merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: For taking the capital and securing Jiankang he received the marquisate of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 從伐廣固，破盧循，隨劉藩追斬徐道覆，與王鎮惡襲江陵，隨朱齡石伐蜀，又從伐司馬休之。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Guanggu, broke Lu Xun, followed Liu Fan in pursuit and beheading Xu Daofu, with Wang Zhen'e raided Jiangling, followed Zhu Lingshi against Shu, and again followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Guanggu, routed Lu Xun, hunted Xu Daofu with Liu Fan, raided Jiangling with Wang Zhen'e, marched on Shu with Zhu Lingshi, and campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 自從征討，凡百餘戰，身被重創。

translations.literal: From following campaigns and punitive expeditions there were over a hundred battles; his body bore grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: In more than a hundred battles his body was crisscrossed with deep wounds.

sentences.zh: 武帝錄其前後功，封新寧縣男。

translations.literal: The Emperor recorded his former and later merit and enfeoffed him Baron of Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tallied his lifetime of service and made him baron of Xinning.

sentences.zh: 武帝北伐，留恩侍衛世子，命朝士與之交。

translations.literal: On the northern expedition the Emperor left En to attend the heir; he ordered courtiers to associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern march the emperor left En to guard the heir and told courtiers to befriend him.

sentences.zh: 恩益自謙損，與人語常呼官位，自稱鄙人，撫士卒甚有恩紀。

translations.literal: En became all the more modest; speaking with others he always used their titles and called himself a rustic; he treated soldiers with great kindness and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He grew humbler still, addressed everyone by rank and called himself a countryman, and treated his men with firm kindness.

sentences.zh: 世子開府，再遷為司馬。

translations.literal: When the heir opened his headquarters En was twice promoted to marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir opened a headquarters En rose twice to marshal.

sentences.zh: 後入關迎桂陽公義真，沒于赫連勃勃。

translations.literal: Later entering the pass to welcome Duke Yizhen of Guiyang he perished at Helian Bobo's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Later, entering the pass to escort Duke Yizhen of Guiyang, he died at the hands of Helian Bobo.

sentences.zh: 傳國至孫，無子，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed to a grandson; without sons the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief passed to a grandson; with no heirs it lapsed.

sentences.zh: 向靖字奉仁，小字彌，河內山陽人也。

translations.literal: Xiang Jing, styled Fengren, pet name Mi, was a man of Shanyang in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Jing, courtesy name Fengren, childhood name Mi, came from Shanyang in Henei.

sentences.zh: 名與武帝祖諱同，故以小字行。

translations.literal: His name matched the taboo of the Emperor's grandfather, so he was known by the pet name.
translations.idiomatic: His given name tabooed the emperor's grandfather, so he went by his childhood name Mi.

sentences.zh: 彌與武帝有舊，從平京城，參建武軍事，進平建鄴，以功封山陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Mi had old ties with the Emperor; he followed in pacifying the capital, served on the staff of the army that established might, advanced to pacify Jiankang, and for merit was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had known the emperor long; he helped take the capital, served on the founding army staff, helped secure Jiankang, and earned the fifth-rank marquisate of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 又從征廣固，討盧循，所在著績，封安南縣男。

translations.literal: He again followed the Guanggu campaign and the Lu Xun punitive action; wherever he went he showed merit and was enfeoffed Baron of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Guanggu and against Lu Xun, distinguishing himself everywhere, and received the barony of Annan.

sentences.zh: 武帝西伐司馬休之，征關中，並見任使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi and on the Guanzhong expedition he was both employed in trust.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and the Guanzhong expedition he was repeatedly entrusted with command.

sentences.zh: 及帝受命，以佐命功，封曲江縣侯，位太子左衛率，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the mandate, for founding merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Qujiang, made Left Commandant of the Heir's Guard, and given concurrent Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynastic founding he became marquis of Qujiang, left commandant of the heir's guard, and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 彌立身儉約，不營室宇，無園田商貨之業，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Mi in person was frugal, did not build houses, had no gardens, fields, or trading business—the age praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply, built no mansion, owned no land or trade, and was widely admired for it.

sentences.zh: 子植嗣，多過失，不受母訓，奪爵。

translations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded but had many faults, would not obey his mother's instruction, and lost the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded but was dissolute, disobeyed his mother, and forfeited the fief.

sentences.zh: 更以植次弟楨紹封，又坐殺人，國除。

translations.literal: The next younger brother Zhen was enfeoffed in his stead; he again was punished for killing a man and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zhen inherited next but was stripped after a murder.

sentences.zh: 楨弟柳字玄季，有學義才能，立身方雅。

translations.literal: Zhen's younger brother Liu styled Xuanji had learning, righteousness, and talent, and conducted himself with upright elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's brother Liu, styled Xuanji, was learned, capable, and upright.

sentences.zh: 太尉袁淑、司空徐湛之、東揚州刺史顏竣皆與友善。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yuan Shu, Minister of Works Xu Tanzhi, and Eastern Yangzhou Inspector Yan Jun were all friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Yuan Shu, Minister of Works Xu Tanzhi, and Eastern Yangzhou inspector Yan Jun counted him a friend.

sentences.zh: 及竣貴，柳猶以素情自許，不推先之。

translations.literal: When Jun rose high Liu still claimed old friendship and did not defer first.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun grew powerful Liu still treated him as an equal of old.

sentences.zh: 順陽范璩誡柳曰：「名位不同，禮有異數，卿何得作曩時意邪？

translations.literal: Shunyang Fan Quan admonished Liu, "Rank and standing differ and ritual has its gradations—how can you act as in former days?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Quan of Shunyang warned him, "Your ranks no longer match—how can you behave as before?

sentences.zh: 」柳曰：「我與士遜心期久矣，豈可一旦以勢利處之。

translations.literal: " Liu said, "Shiyu and I pledged hearts long ago—how can I suddenly treat him by power and profit?
translations.idiomatic: " Liu replied, "Shiyu and I swore friendship long ago—I will not bow to his new power.

sentences.zh: 」及柳為南康郡，涉義宣事敗，系建康獄。

translations.literal: " When Liu was Administrator of Nankang and was implicated in Yixuan's affair and failed, he was imprisoned at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: " When implicated in Yixuan's rebellion as administrator of Nankang, he was jailed at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 屢密請竣，

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent secret pleas to Jun,
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly begged Jun in secret

sentences.zh: 求相申救。

translations.literal: asking him to speak in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: to plead for his life.

sentences.zh: 孝武嘗與竣言及柳事，竟不助之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu once spoke with Jun about Liu's affair, yet in the end did not help him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu discussed Liu's case with Jun but would not intervene.

sentences.zh: 柳遂伏法。

translations.literal: Liu was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was executed.

sentences.zh: 璩字伯玉，平北將軍汪曾孫也，位淮南太守。

translations.literal: Quan styled Boyu, great-grandson of General Who Pacifies the North Wang, and reached the post of Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan, courtesy name Boyu, was great-grandson of General Who Pacifies the North Wang and became administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 劉鍾字世之，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhong, styled Shizhi, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong, courtesy name Shizhi, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 少孤，依鄉人中山太守劉回共居，常慷慨於貧賤。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth he lived with fellow townsman Zhongshan Administrator Liu Hui and often spoke boldly despite poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he lodged with Liu Hui, administrator of Zhongshan, and spoke boldly despite their poverty.

sentences.zh: 從宋武帝征伐，盡其心力。

translations.literal: He followed Song Emperor Wu on punitive expeditions and gave all his heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on campaign and gave everything he had.

sentences.zh: 及義旗建，帝板鍾為郡主簿，曰：「豫是彭城鄉人赴義者，並可依劉主簿。

translations.literal: When the banner of righteousness was raised the Emperor appointed Zhong commandery chief clerk, saying, "All Pengcheng townsmen who join the cause may follow Chief Clerk Liu.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt began the emperor made Zhong chief clerk of the commandery, saying, "Every Pengcheng man who joins us may follow Chief Clerk Liu.

sentences.zh: 」於是立義隊，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon a righteous company was formed and battle after battle was won.
translations.idiomatic: " A loyalist band formed and won every fight.

sentences.zh: 及桓謙屯於東陵，卞範之屯覆舟山西，武帝疑賊有伏兵，顧左右，政見鍾，謂曰：「此山下當有伏兵，卿可往探之。

translations.literal: When Huan Qian garrisoned Dongling and Bian Fanzhi garrisoned west of Fuzhou Mountain the Emperor suspected ambush; looking about he saw only Zhong and said, "Below this mountain there must be hidden troops—you can go probe them.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting ambush below Dongling, the emperor spotted Zhong and said, "There are troops hidden on that slope—go scout them.

sentences.zh: 」鍾馳進，果有伏兵，一時奔走。

translations.literal: " Zhong galloped forward; indeed there were hidden troops who at once fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong charged; hidden troops scattered at once.

sentences.zh: 後除南齊國內史，封安丘縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Later he was made interior minister of Nanqi and enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He later became interior minister of Nanqi and received the fifth-rank marquisate of Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 求改葬父祖及親屬十喪，帝厚加資給。

translations.literal: He asked to rebury father, grandfather, and ten kin; the Emperor richly supplied funds.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to rebury father, grandfather, and ten kin; the emperor funded it generously.

sentences.zh: 從征廣固，孟龍符於陣陷沒，鍾直入取其屍而反。

translations.literal: On the Guanggu campaign Meng Longfu fell in battle; Zhong went straight in and brought back the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Longfu fell at Guanggu, Zhong charged in and retrieved his body.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼建鄴，鍾拒柵，身被重創，賊不得入。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed Jiankang Zhong held the palisade, took grave wounds, and the bandits could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened Jiankang, Zhong held the stakes, badly wounded, and kept the rebels out.

sentences.zh: 循南走，鍾又隨劉藩追徐道覆，斬之。

translations.literal: Xun fled south; Zhong again followed Liu Fan in pursuit of Xu Daofu and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun fled south he hunted Xu Daofu with Liu Fan and killed him.

sentences.zh: 後隨朱齡石伐蜀為前鋒，去成都二百里，鍾于時腳疾，齡石乃詣鍾，謀且欲養銳息兵，以伺其隙。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zhu Lingshi against Shu as vanguard; two hundred li from Chengdu Zhong then had foot ailment; Lingshi came to Zhong intending to rest the sharp troops and wait for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on Shu as vanguard with Zhu Lingshi, two hundred li from Chengdu, Zhong was lame; Lingshi came to propose resting the army and waiting for an opening.

sentences.zh: 鍾曰：「不然，前揚言大眾向內水，譙道福不敢舍涪城，今重軍卒至，出其不意，蜀人已破膽矣。

translations.literal: Zhong said, "Not so—earlier we proclaimed the great host was coming by the inner water and Qiao Daofu dared not leave Fucheng; now the heavy army has suddenly arrived and, beyond their expectation, the Shu people are already terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong objected: "We already said the main force would come by the inner river and Qiao Daofu dared not leave Fucheng; now our army appears suddenly and Shu is already terrified.

sentences.zh: 賊今阻兵守險，是其懼不敢戰，非能持久也。

translations.literal: The bandits now block the road and hold the defiles—that is fear and unwillingness to fight, not ability to last long.
translations.idiomatic: They hold the passes because they are afraid to fight, not because they can endure.

sentences.zh: 因其兇懼攻之，其勢必克；

translations.literal: Strike while they are fierce with fear and the momentum must succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Hit them while panic still grips them and we must win;

sentences.zh: 若緩兵，彼將知人虛實，當為蜀子虜耳。

translations.literal: if we delay they will learn our true strength and we will become captives of Shu."
translations.idiomatic: delay and they will gauge us—and we will be Shu's prisoners."

sentences.zh: 」齡石從之，明日，陷其二城，徑平成都。

translations.literal: " Lingshi followed this; next day he took two cities and went straight to pacify Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: " Lingshi agreed; the next day they took two cities and marched straight into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 以廣固功，封永新縣男。

translations.literal: For Guanggu merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: For Guanggu he received the barony of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 虞丘進字豫之，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Yu Qiujin styled Yuzhi was a man of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qiujin, courtesy name Yuzhi, came from Tan in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 少時隨謝玄討苻堅有功，封關內侯。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Xie Xuan against Fu Jian with merit and was enfeoffed Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he fought Fu Jian under Xie Xuan and earned a marquisate within the passes.

sentences.zh: 後從宋武帝征孫恩，頻戰有功。

translations.literal: Later he followed Song Emperor Wu against Sun En and repeatedly won merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned against Sun En with repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 從定建鄴，除燕國內史，封龍川縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Jiankang he was made interior minister of Yan and enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Longchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiankang he became interior minister of Yan and received the fifth-rank marquisate of Longchuan.

sentences.zh: 及盧循逼都，孟昶等議奉天子過江，進廷議不可，面折昶等，武帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital Meng Chang and others debated escorting the Son of Heaven across the river; Jin spoke in court that this could not be and openly refuted Chang and the rest; the Emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital Meng Chang urged evacuating the emperor across the river; Jin argued against it in open court and won the emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 除鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 後隨劉藩斬徐道覆。

translations.literal: Later he followed Liu Fan in beheading Xu Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Liu Fan in killing Xu Daofu.

sentences.zh: 義熙九年，以前後功，封望蔡縣男。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi, for former and later merit, he was enfeoffed Baron of Wangcai.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 9 he received the barony of Wangcai for lifetime service.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，累遷太子右衛率。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu he rose repeatedly to Right Commandant of the Heir's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 2 he rose to right commandant of the heir's guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，追論討司馬休之功，進爵為子。

translations.literal: On death his merit against Sima Xiuzhi was recalled and he was advanced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: After death his campaign against Sima Xiuzhi was remembered and he was raised posthumously to viscount.

sentences.zh: 傳國至曾孫，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed to a great-grandson; when Qi received the abdication the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief passed to a great-grandson; when Qi took the throne it lapsed.

sentences.zh: 孟懷玉，平昌安丘人也，世居京口。

translations.literal: Meng Huaiyu was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang and for generations resided at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Huaiyu of Anqiu in Pingchang came from a Jingkou family.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝東伐孫恩，以為建武司馬。

translations.literal: When Song Emperor Wu campaigned east against Sun En he was made marshal of the army that established might.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched east against Sun En he became marshal of the army that established might.

sentences.zh: 豫義旗，從平京口，定建鄴，以功封鄱陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He joined the banner of righteousness, followed in pacifying Jingkou and settling Jiankang, and for merit was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the revolt, helped take Jingkou and Jiankang, and received the fifth-rank marquisate of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 盧循逼都，以戰功為中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, for battle merit he was made advising aide in the central army.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital he became an advising aide in the central army for battlefield merit.

sentences.zh: 循平，封陽豐縣男，位江州刺史、南中郎將。

translations.literal: When Xun was pacified he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangfeng, and held the posts of Inspector of Jiangzhou and General of the Southern Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun's defeat he became baron of Yangfeng, inspector of Jiangzhou, and General of the Southern Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: Without sons the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons and the fief lapsed.

sentences.zh: 懷玉弟龍符，驍果有膽氣，早為武帝所知，以軍功封平昌縣五等子。

translations.literal: Huaiyu's younger brother Longfu was fierce and bold with courage; the Emperor knew him early and for military merit enfeoffed him Fifth-rank Viscount of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyu's brother Longfu was daring and fierce; known early to the emperor, he earned the fifth-rank viscounty of Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 從伐廣固，以車騎參軍加龍驤將軍、廣川太守。

translations.literal: Following the Guanggu campaign he was chariot-and-horse aide plus Flying Dragon General and Administrator of Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Guanggu he served as chariot aide, Flying Dragon General, and administrator of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追奔，被圍見害，追贈青州刺史，封臨沅縣男。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout he was surrounded and killed; posthumously he was given Inspector of Qingzhou and enfeoffed Baron of Linjiang.
