translations.idiomatic: Pursuing fleeing enemies he was surrounded and killed; posthumously he became inspector of Qingzhou and baron of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 胡藩字道序，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Hu Fan, styled Daoxu, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fan, courtesy name Daoxu, came from Nanchang in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，居喪以毀聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, his mourning for parents was famed for self-injury.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was famed for grieving himself sick over his parents.

sentences.zh: 太守韓伯見之，謂藩叔尚書少廣曰：「卿此侄當以義烈成名。

translations.literal: Administrator Han Bo saw him and said to Fan's uncle, Minister of the Masters of Writing Shaoguang, "Your nephew will make his name through righteous valor.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Han Bo told Fan's uncle Shaoguang, minister of the masters of writing, "This nephew will win fame by loyal courage.

sentences.zh: 」州府辟不就，須二弟冠婚畢，乃參郗恢征虜軍事。

translations.literal: " The province and prefecture summoned him but he would not go until his two younger brothers had capped and married; then he joined Xi Huai's staff against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused summons until his two brothers were married, then joined Xi Huai's staff.

sentences.zh: 時殷仲堪為荊州刺史，藩外兄羅企生為仲堪參軍。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Zhongkan was Inspector of Jingzhou; Fan's maternal cousin Luo Qisheng was Zhongkan's aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan was then inspector of Jingzhou; Fan's cousin Luo Qisheng served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 藩過江陵省企生，因說仲堪曰：「桓玄意趣不常，節下崇待太過，非將來計也。

translations.literal: Fan crossed to Jiangling to visit Qisheng and therefore said to Zhongkan, "Huan Xuan's intent is inconstant; my lord favors him excessively—this is no plan for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Qisheng at Jiangling, Fan warned Zhongkan, "Huan Xuan is unpredictable—you honor him too highly for your own good.

sentences.zh: 」仲堪不悅。

translations.literal: " Zhongkan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongkan took offense.

sentences.zh: 藩退謂企生曰：「倒戈授人，必至大禍，不早去，後悔無及。

translations.literal: Fan withdrew and told Qisheng, "To turn your blade over to another must bring great disaster—leave early or regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Fan told Qisheng privately, "Handing your sword to another invites ruin—leave now or regret it forever.

sentences.zh: 」後玄自夏口襲仲堪，藩參玄後軍軍事。

translations.literal: " Later Xuan from Xiakou struck Zhongkan; Fan served on Xuan's rear-army staff.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xuan struck from Xiakou, Fan served on his rear-army staff.

sentences.zh: 仲堪敗，企生果以附從及禍。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was defeated; Qisheng indeed perished for following and sharing the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan fell; Qisheng died for staying loyal to him.

sentences.zh: 藩轉參太尉大將軍相國軍事。

translations.literal: Fan was transferred to staff officer on the Grand Marshal's and Chancellor's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan moved to staff duty under the grand marshal and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝起兵，玄戰敗將出奔，藩扣馬曰：「今羽林射手猶有八百，皆是義故西人，一旦舍此，欲歸可復得乎？

translations.literal: When Song Emperor Wu raised troops Xuan was defeated and about to flee; Fan seized his horse and said, "The palace archers still number eight hundred—all old followers from the west; once you abandon this, can you ever return?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rose, Xuan prepared to flee; Fan grabbed his bridle: "You still have eight hundred western archers—leave now and you can never come back.

sentences.zh: 」玄直以鞭指天而已。

translations.literal: " Xuan merely pointed heavenward with his whip.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan only gestured skyward with his whip.

sentences.zh: 於是奔散相失，追及玄於蕪湖。

translations.literal: Thereupon they scattered and lost one another; he caught up with Xuan at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: They scattered in chaos; Fan caught Xuan again at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 玄見藩喜謂張須無曰：「卿州故為多士，今復見王修。

translations.literal: Xuan saw Fan and said joyfully to Zhang Xu Wu, "Your province truly breeds many scholars—now I see Wang Xiu again.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Fan, Xuan told Zhang Xu Wu, "Your region breeds real men—here is Wang Xiu again.

sentences.zh: 」桑落之敗，藩艦被燒，並鎧入水，潛行三十許步，方得登岸。

translations.literal: " At the defeat of Sangluo Fan's ship was burned; wearing armor he entered the water and stole thirty paces before he could climb ashore.
translations.idiomatic: " At Sangluo his ship burned; armored, he swam thirty paces underwater before reaching shore.

sentences.zh: 乃還家。

translations.literal: He then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home.

sentences.zh: 武帝素聞藩直言于殷氏，又為玄盡節，召參鎮軍軍事。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long heard Fan's blunt words to the Yin clan and his full loyalty to Xuan; he summoned him to staff the army that pacifies the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, knowing Fan had warned Yin and served Xuan faithfully, summoned him to the pacifying army staff.

sentences.zh: 從征慕容超，超軍屯聚臨朐。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Murong Chao, Chao's army gathered at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Murong Chao, he found Chao's army massed at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 藩言于武帝曰：「賊屯軍城外，留守必寡，今往取其城而斬其旗幟，此韓信所以克趙也。

translations.literal: Fan said to the Emperor, "The bandits camp outside the city—the garrison must be thin; go now, take the city and cut down their banners—this is how Han Xin conquered Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fan told the emperor, "They camp outside—the city is empty; seize it and strike down their flags, as Han Xin did at Zhao.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃遣檀韶與藩潛往，即克其城。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then sent Tan Shao and Fan secretly; they at once took the city.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Tan Shao and Fan by stealth and they captured it at once.

sentences.zh: 賊見城陷，一時奔走，還保廣固。

translations.literal: The bandits saw the city fall and at once fled, returning to hold Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city lost, the enemy fled back to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 圍之，將拔之夜，忽有鳥大如鵝，蒼黑色，飛入帝帳裏，眾以為不祥。

translations.literal: Besieging it, on the night it was about to fall suddenly a bird large as a goose, dark blue-black, flew into the Emperor's tent; the crowd thought it ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of victory a goose-sized dark bird flew into the imperial tent; men took it for a bad sign.

sentences.zh: 藩賀曰：「蒼黑者，胡虜色。

translations.literal: Fan congratulated him, "Dark blue is the color of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Fan declared, "Dark blue is the barbarians' color.

sentences.zh: 胡虜歸我，大吉之祥。

translations.literal: Barbarians returning to us is a great auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Their surrender is a great omen.

sentences.zh: 」明旦攻城，陷之。

translations.literal: " At dawn he attacked the city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: " At dawn they stormed the city and took it.

sentences.zh: 從討盧循于左裏，頻戰有功，封吳平縣五等子。

translations.literal: Following the punitive action against Lu Xun at Zuoli he repeatedly won merit and was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Viscount of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting Lu Xun at Zuoli he won repeated honors and received the fifth-rank viscounty of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 尋除鄱陽太守，從伐劉毅。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Administrator of Poyang and followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became administrator of Poyang and marched against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，毅當之荊州，表求東道還建鄴辭墓。

translations.literal: At first when Yi was going to Jing Province he memorialized asking to travel the eastern route back to Jiankang to visit his ancestors' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi left for Jing Province he asked to swing by Jiankang to mourn at his family tombs.

sentences.zh: 去都數十里，不過拜闕。

translations.literal: Several tens of li from the capital he did not pass to bow at the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped tens of li from court without paying homage at the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝出倪塘會毅，藩請殺之，乃謂帝曰：「公謂劉衛軍為公下乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor went out to Nitang to meet Yi; Fan asked to kill him and said to the Emperor, "Do you think Defender Liu serves under you?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor met Yi at Nitang; Fan urged killing him: "Do you think Defender Liu serves under you?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿謂何如？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "What do you think?

sentences.zh: 「對曰：「夫豁達大度，功高天下，連百萬之眾，允天人之望，毅固以此服公。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Broad-minded and magnanimous, merit high under heaven, commanding millions, fulfilling heaven and men's hopes—Yi for this submits to you.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan answered, "Your breadth and achievement command the realm—Yi submits to that.

sentences.zh: 至於涉獵記傳，一詠一談，自許以雄豪，加以誇伐，搢紳白麵之士，輻湊而歸，此毅不肯為公下也。

translations.literal: As for browsing records and histories, reciting and conversing, styling himself a hero and adding boast—gentry and pale-faced scholars flock to him; this is Yi refusing to serve under you.
translations.idiomatic: But his salons, his poetry, his swagger—scholars flock to him. That is Yi refusing to serve under you.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾與毅俱有克復功，其過未彰，不可自相圖。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said, "Yi and I both have merit in restoration; his fault is not yet clear—we cannot plot against each other.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "We both restored the dynasty; his disloyalty is not yet proven—we cannot turn on each other.

sentences.zh: 」至是謂藩曰：「昔從卿倪塘之謀，無今舉也。」

translations.literal: " Now he said to Fan, "Had I followed your Nitang counsel there would be no present campaign."
translations.idiomatic: " Now he told Fan, "If I had listened at Nitang I would not need this war."

sentences.zh: 又從征司馬休之，復為參軍。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and again served as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He again campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 徐逵之敗沒，帝怒，即日於馬頭岸度江。

translations.literal: When Xu Daizhi was defeated and lost the Emperor was angry and that same day crossed the Yangzi at Matou bank.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Daizhi's defeat the furious emperor crossed the Yangzi that same day at Matou.

sentences.zh: 江津岸壁立數丈，休之臨岸置陣，無由可登。

translations.literal: The river crossing's bank was a cliff several zhang; Xiuzhi set battle lines on the bank with no way to climb.
translations.idiomatic: The bank rose sheer for yards; Xiuzhi lined the top and offered no foothold.

sentences.zh: 帝呼藩令上，藩有疑色。

translations.literal: The Emperor called Fan to ascend; Fan showed hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fan up; Fan hesitated.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命左右錄來，欲斬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor in anger ordered attendants to seize him and was about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor had him seized for execution.

sentences.zh: 藩不受命，顧曰：「寧前死耳。

translations.literal: Fan would not obey the order and looked back, saying, "Better die going forward.
translations.idiomatic: Fan refused and said, "I would rather die advancing.

sentences.zh: 」以刀頭穿岸，劣容腳指徑上，隨之者稍多。

translations.literal: " He pierced the bank with the sword-point, barely fitting his toes, and went up; those who followed gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: " He dug toeholds with his sword tip and climbed; others followed.

sentences.zh: 及登，殊死戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Once atop they fought to the death and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the top they fought desperately and routed Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 從伐關中，參太尉軍事，統別軍至河東。

translations.literal: Following the Guanzhong expedition he was staff officer on the Grand Marshal's military affairs, commanding a separate army to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On the Guanzhong expedition he led a detached force to Hedong under the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 暴風漂輜重艦度北岸，魏軍牽得此艦。

translations.literal: A gale blew supply ships across to the north bank; Wei troops towed away this ship.
translations.idiomatic: A storm blew a supply ship to the north bank where Wei seized it.

sentences.zh: 藩氣憤，率左右十二人乘小船徑往。

translations.literal: Fan in fury led twelve men in a small boat straight there.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Fan took twelve men in a skiff straight after it.

sentences.zh: 魏騎五六百，見藩來並笑之。

translations.literal: Five or six hundred Wei horsemen saw Fan coming and all laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six hundred Wei cavalry saw him and laughed.

sentences.zh: 藩素善射，登岸射之，應弦而倒者十許人。

translations.literal: Fan had long been skilled at archery; ashore he shot them and over ten fell at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: A fine archer, he shot from shore and dropped a dozen at once.

sentences.zh: 魏軍皆退，悉收所失而反。

translations.literal: The Wei army all retreated and he fully recovered what was lost and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei riders fled and he recovered everything.

sentences.zh: 又遣藩及朱超石等追魏軍於半城，魏騎數萬合圍，藩及超石不盈五千，力戰，大破之。

translations.literal: He again sent Fan and Zhu Chao shi and others to pursue Wei forces at Bancheng; tens of thousands of Wei horsemen surrounded them; Fan and Chao shi had fewer than five thousand and fought fiercely, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fan and Zhu Chao shi after Wei at Bancheng; though surrounded by tens of thousands with fewer than five thousand men they smashed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 武帝還彭城，參相國軍事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to Pengcheng he served on the Chancellor's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Pengcheng he joined the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 論平司馬休之及廣固功，封陽山縣男。

translations.literal: Recalling merit in pacifying Sima Xiuzhi and at Guanggu he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangshan.
translations.idiomatic: For Xiuzhi and Guanggu he received the barony of Yangshan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，位太子左衛率。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia he reached Left Commandant of the Heir's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia he became left commandant of the heir's guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰壯侯。

translations.literal: On death posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子隆世嗣。

translations.literal: Longshi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Longshi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 藩諸子多不遵法度，第十四子遵世同孔熙先逆謀，文帝以藩功臣，不欲顯其事，使江州以他事殺之。

translations.literal: Fan's many sons mostly did not keep the law; the fourteenth son Zunshi joined Kong Xixian's treason; Emperor Wen, because Fan was a founding minister, did not wish the affair exposed and had Jiangzhou kill him on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Fan's sons were unruly; fourteenth son Zunshi joined Kong Xixian's plot, and Emperor Wen had Jiangzhou execute him on a pretext to spare the founder's name.

sentences.zh: 十六子誕世，十七子茂世，後欲奉庶人義康，交州刺史檀和之至豫章討平之。

translations.literal: The sixteenth son Danshi and seventeenth son Maoshi later tried to support the commoner Yikang; Jiao Province Inspector Tan He reached Yuzhang and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth son Danshi and seventeenth Maoshi later backed Prince Yikang; Tan He of Jiao Province crushed them at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 劉康祖，彭城呂人也，世居京口。

translations.literal: Liu Kangzu was a man of Lu in Pengcheng and for generations resided at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kangzu of Lu in Pengcheng came from a Jingkou family.

sentences.zh: 父虔之，輕財好施，位江夏相。

translations.literal: His father Qianzhi lightly valued wealth and loved giving; he reached the post of Chancellor of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianzhi was generous and open-handed and rose to chancellor of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝西征司馬休之及魯宗之，宗之子軌襲殺虔之，追贈梁、秦二州刺史，封新康縣男。

translations.literal: When Song Emperor Wu campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, Zongzhi's son Gui murdered Qianzhi; posthumously Qianzhi was given Inspector of Liang and Qin and enfeoffed Baron of Xinkang.
translations.idiomatic: During the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Lu Zongzhi's son Gui murdered Qianzhi; posthumously he was made inspector of Liang and Qin and baron of Xinkang.

sentences.zh: 康祖便弓馬，膂力絕人，以浮蕩蒱酒為事。

translations.literal: Kangzu was skilled with bow and horse; muscle strength surpassed others; he made a living in reckless gambling and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu excelled at bow and saddle and lived by gambling and wine.

sentences.zh: 每犯法為郡縣所錄，輒越屋踰牆，莫之能禽。

translations.literal: Each time he broke the law and was arrested by commandery or county he would leap over roofs and walls and none could seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever arrested he vaulted rooftops and escaped every pursuer.

sentences.zh: 夜入人家，為有司所圍，突圍去，並莫敢追，因夜還京口，半夕便至。

translations.literal: Entering others' houses at night, when officials surrounded him he broke out and none dared pursue; he returned to Jingkou the same night and by midnight was there.
translations.idiomatic: Caught raiding a house at night, he broke out unscathed, raced to Jingkou, and arrived before midnight.

sentences.zh: 明旦守門詣府州要職，俄而建康移書錄之，府州執事者並證康祖其夕在京口，遂得無恙。

translations.literal: Next dawn he waited at the gate for important posts at prefecture and commandery; soon Jiankang sent documents to arrest him and prefecture and commandery officers all testified Kangzu had been at Jingkou that night, so he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he showed up for official business; when Jiankang ordered his arrest, local officers swore he had been in Jingkou that night and he walked free.

sentences.zh: 前後屢被糾劾，文帝以勳臣子每原貸之。

translations.literal: Repeatedly impeached, Emperor Wen as the son of a merit minister each time pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly impeached, Emperor Wen kept pardoning him as a founder's son.

sentences.zh: 後襲封拜員外郎，再坐蒱戲免官。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the fief and was made Outer Court Gentleman; twice he was removed for gambling.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the fief, became an outer court gentleman, and twice lost office for gambling.

sentences.zh: 孝武為豫州刺史，鎮曆陽，以康祖為征虜中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu as Inspector of Yuzhou garrisoned Liyang and made Kangzu middle army aide against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu held Yuzhou at Liyang he made Kangzu middle army aide.

sentences.zh: 既被委任，折節自修。

translations.literal: Once entrusted he restrained himself and reformed his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Given responsibility he straightened up.

sentences.zh: 曆南平王鑠安蠻府司馬。

translations.literal: He served as marshal of Prince Shuo of Nanping's staff for pacifying the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He served as marshal on Prince Shuo of Nanping's barbarian-pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，魏太武帝親率大眾攻圍汝南，文帝遣諸軍救援，康祖總統為前驅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia Wei Emperor Taiwu personally led a great host to besiege Runan; Emperor Wen sent armies to rescue and Kangzu commanded the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 27 Wei Emperor Taiwu besieged Runan; Emperor Wen sent relief armies with Kangzu in the van.

sentences.zh: 次新蔡，攻破魏軍，去懸瓠四十里。

translations.literal: Newly at Xincai he broke the Wei army, forty li from Xuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Camping at Xincai he routed Wei forty li from Xuanchi.

sentences.zh: 太武燒營而還。

translations.literal: Taiwu burned camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu burned his camp and retreated.

sentences.zh: 轉左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 文帝欲大舉北侵，康祖以歲月已晚，請待明年。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen wished a great northern invasion; Kangzu said the months were already late and asked to wait until next year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen planned a major northern invasion; Kangzu urged waiting until the next year.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，蕭斌、王玄謨、沈慶之等入河，康祖率豫州軍出許、洛。

translations.literal: That autumn Xiao Bin, Wang Xuanmo, Shen Qingzhi, and others entered the Yellow River; Kangzu led Yuzhou troops out toward Xu and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Xiao Bin, Wang Xuanmo, and Shen Qingzhi entered the Yellow River while Kangzu led Yuzhou troops toward Xu and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 玄謨等敗歸，南平王鑠在壽陽，上慮為魏所圍，召康祖速反。

translations.literal: When Xuanmo and the rest were defeated and returned Prince Shuo of Nanping was at Shouyang; the Emperor feared Wei would surround him and summoned Kangzu to return quickly.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanmo's defeat Prince Shuo at Shouyang seemed trapped; the emperor ordered Kangzu back at once.

sentences.zh: 康祖回軍，未至壽陽數十里，會魏永昌王以長安之眾八萬騎，與康祖相及于尉武。

translations.literal: Kangzu turned the army; not yet tens of li from Shouyang he met Wei Prince Yongchang with eighty thousand horsemen from Chang'an at Yuwu.
translations.idiomatic: Marching back, still miles from Shouyang, he met Prince Yongchang of Wei with eighty thousand Chang'an cavalry at Yuwu.

sentences.zh: 康祖有八千人，乃結車營而進。

translations.literal: Kangzu had eight thousand men and therefore formed wagon camp and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: With eight thousand men he locked wagons and advanced.

sentences.zh: 魏軍四面來攻，眾分為三，且休且戰。

translations.literal: Wei forces attacked from four sides; the host divided into three parts, resting and fighting by turns.
translations.idiomatic: Wei attacked from all sides; his men fought in three rotating shifts.

sentences.zh: 康祖率厲將士，無不一當百，魏軍死者太半，流血沒踝。

translations.literal: Kangzu roused officers and soldiers—none did not match one hundred; Wei dead were more than half, blood flooding to the ankles.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu drove his men to fight one against a hundred; half the Wei army died and blood reached their ankles.

sentences.zh: 矢中頭而死，於是大敗，舉營淪覆，免者裁數十人。

translations.literal: An arrow struck his head and he died; thereupon great defeat—the whole camp collapsed and only several tens escaped.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow took his head; the camp collapsed and only dozens escaped.

sentences.zh: 魏人傳康祖首示彭城，面如生。

translations.literal: Wei men displayed Kangzu's head at Pengcheng; his face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Wei paraded his head at Pengcheng; his face looked alive.

sentences.zh: 贈益州刺史，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Inspector of Yi and posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made inspector of Yi with the title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 康祖伯父簡之，有志幹，為宋武帝所知。

translations.literal: Kangzu's uncle Jianzhi had will and capacity and was known to Song Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu's uncle Jianzhi was capable and known to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝將謀興復，收集才力之士，嘗再造簡之，會有客。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to plot restoration and gather men of talent and strength he twice visited Jianzhi when a guest was present.
translations.idiomatic: Planning restoration, the emperor visited Jianzhi twice while guests were there.

sentences.zh: 簡之悟其意，謂虔之曰：「劉下邳再來，必當有意。

translations.literal: Jianzhi understood his intent and told Qianzhi, "Lord Liu of Xiapi came again—he must have a purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi read his intent and told Qianzhi, "Lord Liu of Xiapi came again—he wants something.

sentences.zh: 既不得語，汝可試往見之。

translations.literal: Unable to speak with him, you should try going to see him.
translations.idiomatic: He could not speak openly—you should visit him.

sentences.zh: 」及虔之至，武帝已克京口。

translations.literal: " When Qianzhi arrived the Emperor had already taken Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: " When Qianzhi went the emperor had already seized Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 虔之即投義。

translations.literal: Qianzhi at once joined the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi joined the revolt at once.

sentences.zh: 簡之聞之，殺耕牛，會眾以赴之。

translations.literal: Jianzhi hearing this killed a plow-ox, gathered the crowd, and rushed to join.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this Jianzhi slaughtered an ox, rallied neighbors, and rushed to join.

sentences.zh: 位太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He reached the post of advising aide to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to advising aide to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 簡之弟謙之，好學，撰晉紀二十卷，位廣州刺史，太中大夫。

translations.literal: Jianzhi's younger brother Qianzhi loved learning, compiled Jin Annals in twenty juan, and reached Administrator of Guangzhou and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi's brother Qianzhi was a scholar, wrote Jin Annals in twenty scrolls, and became administrator of Guangzhou and palace grand master.

sentences.zh: 簡之子道產，初為無錫令，襲爵晉安縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Jianzhi's son Daocan at first was magistrate of Wuxi and inherited the Fifth-rank Marquisate of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi's son Daocan began as magistrate of Wuxi and inherited the fifth-rank marquisate of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，累遷梁、南秦二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he rose repeatedly to Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin and was given overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 3 he became inspector of Liang and Southern Qin with overall command.

sentences.zh: 在州有惠化。

translations.literal: In the province he had benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the province with humane reform.

sentences.zh: 後為雍州刺史、領甯蠻校尉，加都督，兼襄陽太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Inspector of Yong, held the office of Commander Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was given overall command, and concurrently Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later became inspector of Yong, commander who pacifies the barbarians, and concurrently administrator of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 善於臨職，在雍部政績尤著，蠻夷前後不受化者皆順服，百姓樂業，由此有襄陽樂歌，自道產始也。

translations.literal: Skilled at holding office, in Yong province his achievements were especially notable; barbarians who had long refused civilization all submitted; the people prospered in their work—hence the Xiangyang songs of joy, beginning with Daocan.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in office; barbarians long unsubmissive yielded, the people thrived, and Xiangyang joy-songs began with him.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，諡曰襄侯。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous title Marquis Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office with posthumous title Marquis Xiang.

sentences.zh: 道產澤被西土，及喪還，諸蠻皆備縗絰號哭，追送至於沔口。

translations.literal: Daocan's grace spread through the western lands; when the coffin returned all barbarians wore mourning and wailed, escorting to the Han ford.
translations.idiomatic: When his bier returned, barbarians wore mourning and wailed him to the Han river.

sentences.zh: 三年，南兗州刺史竟陵王誕有罪不受征，延孫馳遣中兵參軍杜幼文赴討。

translations.literal: In the third year Southern Yanzhou Inspector Prince Dan of Jingling was guilty and refused summons; Yansun urgently sent middle army aide Du Youwen to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Prince Dan of Jingling, inspector of Southern Yanzhou, rebelled; Yansun sent Du Youwen against him.

sentences.zh: 及至，誕已閉城自守，乃還。

translations.literal: When they arrived Dan had already shut the city and held out, so they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had already barred the gates; they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 誕遣劉公泰齎書要之，延孫斬公泰，送首建鄴，復遣幼文受沈慶之節度。

translations.literal: Dan sent Liu Gongtai with a letter to win him over; Yansun beheaded Gongtai, sent the head to Jiankang, and again sent Youwen under Shen Qingzhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent Liu Gongtai to recruit him; Yansun executed Gongtai, sent his head to court, and put Youwen under Shen Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔延孫曰：「舊京樹親，由來常准。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict to Yansun said, "The old capital's fief for kin has always been the standard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 an edict told Yansun, "The old capital's fief for imperial kin has always been the rule.

sentences.zh: 今此防久弭，當以還授小兒。

translations.literal: Now this defense has long been quiet—it should be returned to the younger son.
translations.idiomatic: That post has been quiet too long—it should go back to the younger prince.

sentences.zh: 」乃征延孫為侍中、尚書左僕射，領護軍。

translations.literal: " He was then summoned as Palace Attendant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: " Yansun was recalled as palace attendant, left vice director, and Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 延孫病，不任拜赴。

translations.literal: Yansun was ill and could not attend the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, Yansun could not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒，給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: On death he was given Grand Marshal and twenty guard swords.
translations.idiomatic: He died before assuming office and was posthumously made grand marshal with twenty guard swords.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諡忠穆，詔改為文穆。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized posthumous title Zhongmu; an edict changed it to Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed posthumous title Zhongmu; the emperor changed it to Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 子質嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 論曰：劉敬宣與宋武恩結龍潛，義分早合，雖興復之始，事隔逢迎，而深期久要，未之或爽。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Liu Jingxuan and Song Wu were bound in grace while still obscure; their righteous tie was early and firm; though at the start of restoration favor lagged in meeting, their deep long-term pledge never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Liu Jingxuan and Emperor Wu bonded in obscurity; though early restoration kept them apart, their long trust never broke.

sentences.zh: 隆赫之任，遂止於人存，飾終之數，無聞於身後。

translations.literal: Lofty appointments reached only while he lived; honors after death were not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Grand rank came only in life; no posthumous glory followed.

sentences.zh: 恩禮之有厚薄，將別有以乎？

translations.literal: Thick or thin in grace and ritual—was there some distinction intended?
translations.idiomatic: Was the uneven favor in gifts and rites deliberate?

sentences.zh: 劉懷肅、劉懷慎、劉粹、孫處、蒯恩、向靖、劉鍾、虞丘進、孟懷玉、孟龍符、胡藩等，或階緣恩舊，一其心力，或攀附風雲，奮其鱗羽，咸能振拔塵滓，自致封侯。

translations.literal: Liu Huaisu, Liu Huaishen, Liu Cui, Sun Chu, Kuai En, Xiang Jing, Liu Zhong, Yu Qiujin, Meng Huaiyu, Meng Longfu, Hu Fan, and others—some by old kindness gave one heart, some clung to the rising wind and flashed their scales and feathers—all could shake off the mire and win enfeoffment themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu, Huaishen, Cui, Sun Chu, Kuai En, Xiang Jing, Zhong, Yu Qiujin, Huaiyu, Longfu, Hu Fan, and others—some repaid old debts, some rode the rising tide—all climbed from the mud to enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「無德不報」，其言信矣。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "None virtuous goes unrequited"—the words are true.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Virtue is never unrewarded"—truly so.

sentences.zh: 康祖門奉興王，早裂封壤，受委疆埸，赴蹈為期。

translations.literal: Kangzu's house served the rising king, enfeoffed early, entrusted on the frontier, and marched to the death as promised.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu's clan served the founding king, took early fiefs, held the frontier, and died as duty demanded.

sentences.zh: 道產樹績漢南，歷年踰十，遺風餘烈，有足稱焉。

translations.literal: Daocan planted achievement south of Han for more than ten years; lingering wind and remaining blaze are worth naming.
translations.idiomatic: Daocan built merit in the Han south for a decade; his legacy deserves remembrance.

sentences.zh: 覽其行事，可謂異跡均美。

translations.literal: Reviewing their deeds one may call them different tracks of equal beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Their careers differ yet shine equally.

sentences.zh: 延孫隆名盛寵，擇而後授，遂以腹心之托，自致宗臣之重，亦其遇也。

translations.literal: Yansun's lofty name and heavy favor—chosen before conferral—thereby received the trust of the inner heart and rose to the weight of a pillar of the clan; such was his fortune too.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun won great name and favor, was chosen before promotion, earned the emperor's inner trust and pillar status—such was his luck.
